note: BORN NOT FOR SALE 2026-08-25. Every date in this note is read off a dated row or a dated file and named beside it; none of them comes from this machine's clock, which reads two different days depending which setting is asked. WHAT THE LANE DOES. Some appointments are not optional. A California corporation has to name somebody who can be handed a lawsuit on its behalf, and the state's own code limits who that may be, so there is a market of companies selling that service and no neutral place to compare them. The lane builds that comparison table: alphabetical, free to read, free to be listed, free to correct, with every square carrying the company's own sentence and the date they said it. The order is the product. The sorter is never handed the information about who has paid, so paying cannot move anybody, and the lane's own note says a company can only climb the list by renaming itself. NOTHING IS LISTED AND NOTHING HAS BEEN SOLD. Counted read-only out of the lane's own store at revenue-2026/var/provider_table_data.db as this row was written: providers 0, claims 0, changes 0, read_basis 0, lookups 0, log_reads 0, markets 1, renders 2. The one market row carries registered_on 2026-08-24 and conflict_checked_on 2026-08-24 -- the check that asks whether we sell anything into the market we are about to referee, answered 'clear' with its reasons written out. The two render rows are both state 'published', both with providers 0 and paid 0, dated rendered_on 2026-08-24 and rendered_on 2026-08-25, and they carry the same fingerprint as each other because the document did not change between them. WHY NOBODY IS ON IT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE STORY OF THIS PAGE. The lane cannot take the names yet. Its own declaration file rules/provider-list-source.json, written_on 2026-08-25, carries terms_status NOT_READ and an empty subjects list, and records four dated attempts on 2026-08-25 to find the California Secretary of State's own list of the companies that have filed under section 1505: the site's robots file answered with an empty file that forbids nothing, a guessed address for a service-agents page answered 404, the sitemap answered 404, and the home page answered but builds its own navigation with scripts we do not run, which is UNKNOWN and never guessed past. The file's own reason says two separate things are missing and neither is a code problem: the exact address of the state's list has not been found by reading, and nobody has read that site's terms of use. OPERATOR DECISION NEEDED, and this build does not make it: the operator's reading approval at revenue-2026/approvals/read_public_sites.md, status ACTIVE, approved_on 2026-08-25, permits fetching a company's public pages under five written conditions and says in terms that it does not cover where a list of company names may be taken from, and that a machine may write a permission note from evidence but never a permission decision. So this page is built as if the answer were 'not yet', and it says so in words. SAMPLE STATUS IS 'fail' AND NOT 'on-page', FOR THE SAME REASON peak-call GAVE. There is no file behind this page to slice: the table has 0 provider rows, so a sample of it would be an empty file, and the pill saying 'sample not ready' is correct and will stop being correct the day the first company is listed. It is NOT 'on-page' either. On-page is a promise that the whole of what we hold is printed on the page, and that is false here: the lane's published document carries four sentences of California statute quoted word for word out of copies saved on 2026-08-24, and this page deliberately does not reprint them, because nobody has written down whether that text may be republished on our own site and this build may not decide that. The page names each of those four items in plain words, cites the section, says which saved file it was checked against and on what day, and says where the quoted sentences themselves live. Calling that on-page would be a sentence a stranger could check and find untrue. PRICE. The page's price rail says 'Not for sale yet' and that is the whole truth of it: no amount has been set for this page, nobody has been charged, and there is nothing to buy. The lane's own code does carry two possible later products -- a maintained profile and a multi-market one -- each with an amount written into it. Neither has ever been sold, no payment link exists, and neither number is printed on the page or in this note, because a number a reader can see is an offer whether or not we meant it as one. CADENCE. 'a dated version a day so far' is measured, not promised: the store holds exactly two dated versions of the table, 2026-08-24 and 2026-08-25, one day apart, and 'so far' is doing honest work in that sentence. cadence_long is NOT stored in this row on purpose -- scripts/slice_provider_table.py recounts it off the render rows at build time, so the page cannot go stale even if this row does. THE KILL NUMBER IS THE LANE'S, READ NOT TYPED. run.py carries KILL_NUMBER, SELF_LOOKUPS_BY 2026-10-05 and KILL_DATE 2026-11-22, and the page reads all three out of that file with the parser rather than running it. Self-lookups -- a named company loading its own row, proved off a server log -- stand at 0, and none is possible until this page is live somewhere a company could find it. The page says that in words rather than printing a nought and letting it read as a measurement. NO NUMBER, DATE, PRICE, GROUP, CADENCE OR BUYER IS TYPED INTO THE PAGE. scripts/slice_provider_table.py reads group, cadence, buyer and price out of this row with no fallback and refuses to build if any of them is missing, and reads every count, date, column title and sentence out of the lane's store read-only and out of the lane's own source files with the Python parser, never by importing or running them. It recomputes the published document's fingerprint with the lane's own recipe on every build and refuses to write the page if it no longer matches, because the only claim a dated record makes is that it was not edited afterwards. It refuses to build if any row appears in providers, claims, changes, read_basis, lookups or log_reads, because every sentence on the page says there are none. It refuses if the newest published render's own counts disagree with the store's own tables. It refuses if either of the lane's price amounts appears anywhere in the finished page. And it holds the finished page against the shared ranking-word guard, with the lane's own refusal lines exempt once each, proving on every build that the guard both fires on a judging line and clears a plain one. THERE IS NO FORM, NO ACCOUNT AND NO SELF-SERVE ANYTHING. This estate's platform is not ours to add one to. The only way in is an email thread with a person, which is what the contact block says. WIRING, FOR WHOEVER MERGES THIS. One row is added to scripts/family_status.py SOURCES pointing at the lane's store, table renders, column rendered_on, cadence 1 -- the two dated rows are one day apart. renders is the table the page's content comes from: each row holds the rendered document itself and its fingerprint, not a note that a job ran. Without that row the built page would carry no read-date stamp and scripts/check_built.py would mark it as a page with no read date, which is the landmine peak-call's own note warned about. If the lane stops re-rendering, the page will correctly report that its reader has stopped; do not soften the cadence to quieten that.
